headline: Dynamical models connect local regulatory rules to multicellular and network-level…
label: Biological Dynamics Modeling Frameworks
summary: Recent preprints and a published study couple stochastic, spatial and attractor-based simulation with model refinement across scales.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of explicit dynamical models to connect local rules to system-level behavior. A preprint extending a classical gene-regulatory evolution model with noisy developmental dynamics reports that noise favors robust, motif-enriched networks. A Boolean network protocol for osteogenesis removes spurious attractors from a 9-node model, while Evoscope simulates cells on a toroidal lattice under a minimal regulatory grammar, with multicellular morphology emerging. A published Kuramoto study on directed, weighted C. elegans connectomes relates connection weights and directionality to chimera states. A further preprint links oscillatory and linear epigenomic and transcriptomic dynamics in developing mouse, C. elegans and single-cell data, applying the same dynamical framing to temporal trajectories. What is new is the coupling of stochastic and spatial simulation with model-refinement procedures across evolutionary, attractor-based and multicellular scales.
